issues.description: Method name mismatch between StockIngredient and Stock (and comments/Main): the template StockIngredient class exposes retrieveQuantity() but other code (Stock.add/take and example Main in comments) expects getQuantity(). The problem statement instructs students to add getters for private fields and the solution uses getQuantity(), so the template's use of retrieveQuantity() is an unintended structural inconsistency that will cause compilation errors and confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name consistent across the codebase. Replace or add retrieveQuantity() with a public getQuantity() method in StockIngredient (or have getQuantity() delegate to retrieveQuantity()). Ensure all references (Stock, Main, examples, and instructions) use getQuantity(). This aligns the template with the problem statement and the provided solution.

issues.description: The template StockIngredient class defines the quantity accessor as retrieveQuantity(), while the Stock class (template) calls getQuantity() and the problem statement requests standard getters. The solution implementation uses getQuantity(). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual getter (ingredient quantity) across artifacts will confuse students and cause compilation/usage errors when Stock and StockIngredient are used together.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename retrieveQuantity() in the template StockIngredient class to getQuantity(), or add a getQuantity() method that delegates to retrieveQuantity(). This aligns the template with the problem statement and the solution, and ensures Stock can call getQuantity() consistently.
